notes:
I couldn't write these notes. When I tried to read the source pages, the tool failed and then blocked any further tries for this turn. So I haven't read a single page, from Enduring Word, Bible Hub (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit), Precept Austin, Wesley's Notes or any of the other sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point and leave out anything I couldn't find. Since I found nothing, I have nothing I can honestly report for any verse. Writing the commentary from memory would mean making up sources, so I haven't done that.

If you send the request again in a new message, I'll start over. This is the plan, so you can change anything first:

1. **Traditional verse-by-verse reading (vv. 1–27):** Enduring Word on Daniel 9; Precept Austin's Daniel 9 commentary; Bible Hub's pages for each verse (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Barnes, Keil & Delitzsch); and Wesley's Notes on Daniel.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** mostly the "seventy weeks" in vv. 24–27. That covers who the "Messiah… cut off" is, who "he" is in v. 27, and whether the final week has already happened or is still to come. I'd look at:
   - Dispensational and Baptist teachers: gty.org (MacArthur), gotquestions.org, bible.org
   - Reformed teachers: ligonier.org, monergism.com, thegospelcoalition.org
   - Lutheran: lcms.org, 1517.org
   - Wesleyan: wesley.nnu.edu, seedbed.com
   - Pentecostal: enduringword.com, samstorms.org (Storms writes on the seventy weeks from an amillennial view)
3. **Other views:**
   - Modern scholarship: the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey (which usually link vv. 26–27 to the high priest Onias III and Antiochus IV)
   - Catholic and Orthodox: catholic.com, New Advent (Church Fathers and the Catholic Encyclopedia), oca.org
   - Popular modern teaching (prosperity, word of faith, hyper-grace): only if a site actually discusses it in connection with this chapter

It may also work better to do the chapter in two parts, the prayer (vv. 1–19) and then Gabriel and the seventy weeks (vv. 20–27), so each part gets fully covered.
